clue.text: Born fool without one underlying principle

indicators.note: 'without' in its old sense of 'outside', so one thing wraps around another

blocks.note: B is the standard abbreviation for born, as in genealogies
an ass is a fool
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone was a born fool because they had no guiding principle at all.
explanation.walkthrough: I sits inside ASS to make ASIS, after B: BASIS.
explanation.definitionFit: A basis is the foundation or fundamental idea on which something rests.

clue.text: One looking for a good deal — second award winner

definitions.text: One looking for a good deal

blocks.note: a bar is the clasp added to a medal ribbon when the same decoration is won a second time
one who gains is a winner

explanation.surface: A shrewd shopper hunting a bargain turns out to be the runner-up in a prize contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second award winner' reads as a runner-up, but it splits into 'second award' and 'winner'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bargainer haggles over price, trying to secure favourable terms in a purchase.

clue.text: Former statesman presided without notice

indicators.note: 'without' in its old sense of 'outside', so one word is wrapped around another

blocks.note: a chairman who presided sat in the chair
an ad, or advertisement, is a notice

explanation.surface: A one-time politician chaired a meeting without giving anyone any warning.
explanation.walkthrough: Anwar Sadat was President of Egypt from 1970 until his assassination in 1981.
explanation.definitionFit: Sadat was an Egyptian president and Nobel peace laureate, a statesman now dead.

clue.text: One with nothing to lose in cruise at sea — it involves no duties

indicators.note: losing something means it is dropped from the word it belonged to
being at sea is being confused and all over the place, so the letters are jumbled
one piece is placed inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written
the letter O looks like a zero, nothing
taken as written

explanation.surface: A person with nothing to lose on a sea cruise has a job with no duties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At sea' fits the cruise picture but is the jumble signal, and 'One' is the word itself, not a numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: A sinecure is a paid post requiring little or no work, originally a church office without care of souls.

clue.text: Most prestigious prize vessel brought back

indicators.note: bringing something back sends it the way it came, so the letters run in the opposite direction

blocks.note: a prize is a reward
a pot is a vessel

explanation.surface: The most coveted trophy, a prize cup, is brought back home.
explanation.walkthrough: REWARD followed by POT, read backwards as a whole, gives TOP-DRAWER.
explanation.definitionFit: Top-drawer is an idiom for the highest social class or quality, like the best things kept in the top drawer.

clue.text: Attempt to carry article — on this?

definitions.text: Attempt to carry article — on this?

indicators.note: carrying something means holding it within, so one word holds the other

blocks.note: a try is an attempt
the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A question about what you might use when trying to carry an object.
explanation.walkthrough: TRY holding A gives TRAY, and the whole clue also describes it: a flat board you try to carry things on.
explanation.definitionFit: A tray is the flat carrier on which plates, cups and other items are borne.

clue.text: Cheap tins thrown out, seconds showing inconsistency

indicators.note: things thrown out land in disorder, so these letters are scattered and rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
S is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: Cheap tins discarded as seconds, rejects showing uneven quality.
explanation.walkthrough: Seconds are factory rejects, which fits the surface, but here the word yields just one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Patchiness is unevenness, being good in some parts and poor in others.

clue.text: Gunners turn quarters upside down to find bit of their equipment

indicators.note: to turn something over is to flip it end for end
in a down clue, upside down means the word reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: the Royal Artillery, the British Army's gunners
a dorm, or dormitory, is sleeping quarters

explanation.surface: Soldiers turn their barracks upside down hunting for a missing piece of kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Their' points back to the gunners: the definition is a gunner's tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A ramrod is the rod used to push the charge down the barrel of a muzzle-loading gun.

clue.text: Cascading stream is a worry, rising to come through barrier

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the word is read from the bottom upwards
coming through a barrier puts one thing inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written
to fret is to worry
a wall is a barrier

explanation.surface: A rushing stream is a concern as it rises and breaks through a dam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' applies only to the worry, not to 'a'; 'is' simply links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A waterfall is a river or stream falling steeply over a drop, cascading down.

clue.text: It sounds as if revolutionary rebel is kindled anew

indicators.note: the setter flags that we want a word said like another, not spelt like it
a revolution turns something right round, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: Wat Tyler, the rebel who led the Peasants' Revolt of 1381; a tiler, who lays tiles, is said the same

explanation.surface: A rebel's revolutionary spirit is fired up all over again.
explanation.walkthrough: The rebel is Wat Tyler; say his name and write it TILER, then read that backwards to get RELIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Relit is the past participle of relight: set alight again, so kindled a second time.

clue.text: Understand spoilt son is playing truant and not working

indicators.note: something spoilt is damaged and out of shape, so its letters are rearranged
a truant is absent, so this letter goes missing from the word

blocks.note: taken as written
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A parent understands their spoilt son is skipping school and doing no work.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the S out of UNDERSTAND and rearrange the remaining nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Redundant describes someone laid off and so out of a job, or anything no longer needed.

clue.text: Doctor on the phone from the lodge

blocks.note: MO is a Medical Officer, an army doctor
TEL is the abbreviation for telephone, as printed on letterheads

explanation.surface: A doctor makes a call from the porter's lodge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' here only places the doctor next to the phone.
explanation.definitionFit: A motel is roadside lodging for motorists, a kind of lodge where travellers stay.

clue.text: Get off the defensive in what sounds like a change of direction

indicators.note: the setter says we want something that is heard like the phrase that follows

blocks.note: a tack is a sailing ship's change of course into the wind

explanation.surface: A sports commentator describes a team switching from defence to forward play.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken, 'a tack' runs together into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To attack is to take the offensive, the opposite of defending.

clue.text: Officer in command intercepting the deserter is one claiming the highest authority

indicators.note: to intercept is to step in the middle, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: OC is an Officer Commanding, the officer in command of a unit
THE as written, and a rat is one who deserts, like rats leaving a sinking ship

explanation.surface: A commanding officer catches a deserter who insists he answers to a higher power.
explanation.walkthrough: The officer is OC (Officer Commanding), not the more familiar CO. The highest authority claimed is God.
explanation.definitionFit: A theocrat rules or would rule in the name of God, claiming divine authority.

clue.text: One settling things with brief word put an underground worker off

blocks.note: first meaning: one who settles or decides matters
second meaning: in grammar, a short word such as 'a' or 'the' placed before a noun
read as a phrase: to put someone off is to deter them, and a miner is an underground worker

explanation.surface: Someone resolves a dispute with a few curt words, and a pit worker is discouraged.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer splits as DETER + MINER: 'put off' and 'an underground worker', with the miner placed between the two halves of 'put off' in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A determiner decides things; in grammar it is the short word, like an article, that introduces a noun.

clue.text: US city in which one could find real son

blocks.clueFragment: US city in which one could find real son
blocks.note: surface reading: a town where some boy might find his true father
setter's reading: the city's name is itself an instruction, 'new' meaning rearranged, applied to the French city it is named after, and that rearrangement spells 'real son'

explanation.surface: A city in America where a lost son might be found, perhaps a genuine one.
explanation.walkthrough: Reverse the usual anagram: NEW ORLEANS says 'a new version of ORLEANS', and ORLEANS rearranged is REAL SON.
explanation.definitionFit: New Orleans is the Louisiana port city on the Mississippi, home of jazz.

clue.text: Hawk enthusiastic about Germany losing lots

indicators.note: what is lost is taken away from the word before it

blocks.note: warm means enthusiastic, as in a warm welcome
on means about, as in a talk on art
taken as written
many means lots; these are the letters removed

explanation.surface: A militarist keen on Germany is losing heavily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hawk' looks like a verb, as in hawking goods, but it is the political noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A hawk in politics is one who favours war, just as a warmonger stirs up conflict.

clue.text: Worthless supporter turned back at football entrance

indicators.note: something turned back faces the other way, so it is read from right to left
the entrance is the way in, so only the opening letter is wanted

blocks.note: a fan supports a team
the opening letter of football

explanation.surface: A useless fan is turned away at the turnstile of a football ground.
explanation.walkthrough: Naff is British slang for tacky, uncool or rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Naff is a slang adjective for something of poor quality, cheap or worthless.

clue.text: Boxer is only weed one'd knocked out in bout

indicators.note: what is knocked out is removed from the words before it
the remains are placed inside the next word

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, these are the letters removed
a bout is a fight

explanation.surface: A puny boxer is knocked out during the contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weed' means a weakling, which suits a boxer, but here it only supplies letters; each letter of one'd comes out in order.
explanation.definitionFit: A flyweight is a boxer in one of the lightest weight classes, so a boxer by category.

clue.text: Unusually quaint French art in these?

definitions.text: Unusually quaint French art in these?

indicators.note: something done unusually is done out of the normal order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
'tu es' is French for 'thou art'

explanation.surface: Charming old French artworks might be found among these.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Art' is the verb, as in 'thou art', not painting. The whole clue also describes the answer: old curios with unusually quaint French art.
explanation.definitionFit: Antiques are old collectable objects, often quaint, decorated or French-made.

clue.text: Thin slip with article enclosed (rejected)

indicators.note: something enclosed is shut up inside another thing
a thing rejected is sent back, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: to slip is to make a mistake, to err
the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A flimsy slip of paper with an item tucked inside is sent back.
explanation.walkthrough: A goes inside ERR to make ERAR, which is then read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Rare means thin or rarefied, as the rare air at high altitude.

clue.text: Through relation meets friend face to face?

blocks.note: per means through or by means of
a son is a relation
an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: Through a relative, someone meets a friend in person.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by example: meeting face to face is meeting in person.
explanation.definitionFit: Personally means in person, directly, as when two people meet face to face.

clue.text: Wince, being cut up

blocks.note: first meaning: to draw back sharply in pain or fear
second meaning: a variant of flense, to strip the blubber from a whale

explanation.surface: Someone winces because they are upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut up' reads as upset, but it is the whaler's verb for carving up a carcass.
explanation.definitionFit: To flinch is to wince or recoil; as a rare whaling verb it means to slice up a whale.

clue.text: Examine script circling learner's difficulties

indicators.note: circling something means going all round it, so it ends up inside

blocks.note: to probe is to examine
MS is a manuscript, a handwritten script
L is a learner, as on L-plates

explanation.surface: A teacher checks an exam script, ringing a pupil's mistakes.
explanation.walkthrough: The examine and script pieces are joined first, and the pair then circles the learner.
explanation.definitionFit: Problems are difficulties, troubles that need solving.

clue.text: Competes for parking places

blocks.note: P is the parking sign
to lay something is to place it

explanation.surface: Drivers jostle for parking spaces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Places' looks like a noun after 'parking', but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To play is to take part in a game or contest, so plays means competes.

clue.text: Motorway madness may give false impression to the traveller

definitions.text: may give false impression to the traveller

blocks.note: the M1, Britain's first long motorway, written with I for the one
rage is madness, fury

explanation.surface: Road rage on the motorway can mislead a driver.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 runs from London to Leeds; crosswords write it MI.
explanation.definitionFit: A mirage is an optical illusion, such as water seen on a hot road, that deceives a traveller.

clue.text: Active soldier drowning in the drink

indicators.note: something drowning in liquid is submerged inside it

blocks.note: GI is an American soldier
ale is a drink; the word 'the' rides along

explanation.surface: A soldier on active service ends up in the sea, 'the drink'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The drink' is slang for the sea, but here it is simply beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Agile means nimble and lively, quick in movement, and so active.

clue.text: Bank's support leading to introduction of ecu

indicators.note: an introduction comes at the start, so only the opening letter is taken

blocks.note: a bra is a support garment
the first letter of ecu, the European currency unit of the time

explanation.surface: A bank backs the launch of a new European currency.
explanation.walkthrough: Brae is a Scottish word for a hillside or steep bank.
explanation.definitionFit: A brae is a slope or hillside, especially beside a river, so a bank.

clue.text: Technical talk needing no introduction — it's just gas

indicators.note: with no introduction, the opening letter is dropped

blocks.note: jargon is the specialist talk of a trade

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses specialist talk as mere hot air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gas' in the surface means idle chatter; in the answer it is a chemical element.
explanation.definitionFit: Argon is an inert noble gas, element 18, found in the air.

clue.text: Looking after mathematical genius after career set-back

indicators.note: something set back is pushed the other way, so it reads backwards

blocks.note: to career is to run headlong
Alan Turing, the mathematician and wartime codebreaker

explanation.surface: Caring for a brilliant mathematician after a setback in his career.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Career' is the verb, to rush along, not a job.
explanation.definitionFit: Nurturing means caring for and fostering growth, so looking after someone.

clue.text: Cleaner getting all-round sudden increase or one-off extra sum?

indicators.note: being got all round means being surrounded, so one word encloses the other

blocks.note: a char, or charwoman, is a cleaner
a surge is a sudden increase

explanation.surface: A cleaner gets a sudden rise across the board, or maybe just a one-off bonus.
explanation.walkthrough: A char, short for charwoman, is a British cleaning lady.
explanation.definitionFit: A surcharge is an additional charge added on top of the usual price.

clue.text: Two pages placed either side of the man

indicators.note: being on either side of something means wrapping around it

blocks.note: to set is to place
he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: Two page boys stand on either side of the man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pages' suggests attendants, but they are book pages: a single leaf.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheet or leaf of a book has a page on each side, so it carries two pages.
